newsitem.title: UK: Clean tankers depressed, except Caribbean market.
newsitem.headline: Clean tankers depressed, except Caribbean market.

text.p: Clean tanker rates remained in the doldrums this week and brokers said they expected the market to remain soft for at least the next two or three weeks.
Brokers E.A. Gibson said owners were "finding it difficult to secure suitable employment to avoid sitting without any cargo."
"It is unlikely that this current lull will abate until well into next month," they added in their weekly tanker market report.

Middle East rates in particular continued to slip, with 33,000 cargoes to India fixed at W142.5 while 30,000 tonnes cross-Gulf was done for a lump sum as low as $90,000. The Mediterranean market also continued to sag with enquiry barely sufficient to maintain rates at last week's levels, Gibson said.
Cross-Med 28,000/29,000 tonne gas oil cargoes fetched a dismal W150, while naphtha did not fare much better at W177.5
The Caribbean market was the only relatively bright spot, with 30,000 tonnes Caribs/upcoast at around W240, against W140 at this time last year, Gibson said.
"There has been a sufficiency of enquiry into West Coast South and West Coast Central America to enable the market to remain firm at least until the forthcoming month," they added.
The U.K./Cont market was lacklustre, with 28,000/29,000 tonne cargoes from Ventspils at W150 and a high failure rate, brokers said.
